angle: Phone-first reading for a general audience with ADHD. The page is one long tape you scroll down, from ordinary men to the meatball. A to-scale log tape (15 to 1,000) stays pinned beside the figures. Each stop opens with a tape-yellow score tag, a display headline and a one-line verdict, then shows its lineup of flat figures. The desktop layout comes from the same structure: the pinned tape widens into a to-scale overview.
summary:
Proposal: "the tape you scroll down". On a phone a 46 px sticky rail sits at the left. It is a yellow tailor's tape with log graduations from 15 to 1,000, drawn to scale. It marks every build as a coloured tick, shows the empty gaps hatched, draws Kouri's 25 as a dashed line, puts a chalk-blue dotted bracket over 40 to 200 (where the functional limits fall, position not yet worked out) and a chalk circle at 924. A box shows which stop you are reading, and tapping the tape jumps to a stop.

The stops scroll on the right, in this order:
- Ordinary men (up to 25)
- The natural limit (anchor rows)
- Trained hard (25 to 32)
- The biggest humans on record (32 to 41)
- EMPTY (41 to 57)
- Comic giants (57 to 88)
- Where the body stops working (geometry)
- EMPTY (88 to 152)
- Rex and Ollie (152 to 188, drawn larger)
- EMPTY to the top (188 to 924)
- The meatball (924)

After the stops comes the measuring tool, then collapsed Sources / What the score ignores / Review history.

Every lineup stands against the turnarounds' studio wall: a pale blue-grey band, a light floor strip and a dashed top-of-skull line. Every figure is scaled to that line. In the duo stop, the crest and horns rise above it.

The figures in the mock are real geometry, not placeholders. Humans come from build-comparison/src/figure.js human() using calc.js girths (own versus template). Rex and Ollie come from traced(). Only the scores are mock (geometric mid of guessed body-fat ranges), and every number on the page is marked as mock.

The desktop page uses the same parts:
- a two-column masthead
- a sticky control bar with a Go-to menu
- a 330 px sticky overview: the tape plus six group lanes with range bars, hatched EMPTY bands and stop labels with leader lines
- lineups six to a row
- the tool in two columns

A separate styles.html shows the three proposed chart styles on the same seven figures.

styles.figure_treatment: Flat fills, one per group, taken from the turnarounds: studio slate for everyday men, steel teal for natural athletes, Ollie's maroon briefs for bodybuilders, Rex's navy briefs for strongmen and lifters, crest-glint gold (darkened for contrast) for comic characters, umber for Rex and russet for Ollie. Each figure stands in front of the blue-grey wall band, which has a floor strip and a dashed top-of-skull line. The edge marking is an ink stroke drawn under the fill, so only its outer half (about 1.9 px) shows. Arms and hands get a hairline seam in --seam so they read over the torso, the one interior detail, in keeping with the turnarounds' clean contours. Geometry (the widened template and the meatball) is drawn in chalk blue, outline only with a pale fill.
styles.why: It keeps the Build Calculator's tailor's-sheet system (same paper, ink, tape, chalk and fonts), so the two pages read as one family, and brings in the art's own studio wall and floor. Group colour lets a skimming reader see that the giants are all comic characters and that Superman sits among ordinary men, while the edge still carries where each outline came from. It has both themes with checked contrast. A navy/maroon/gold/umber set is not one of the templated AI looks.

styles.why: Closest to the art: the figures look as if they stand in the render. Rejected because white 11 px text on mid-grey is weak (about 3:1), it can't follow the light and dark themes, and the navy and maroon fills sink into the grey.

styles.name: C. Umber print
styles.tokens: LIGHT: --paper:#EEF0EC; --fig:#3A2A20; --edge:#15181C; floor tiles --tile-everyday:#6C6F86; --tile-enhanced:#7A2434; --tile-strong:#232C5C; --tile-comic:#A0650C; --tile-duo:#E0A030 (crest gold). DARK: --paper:#101215; --fig:#D8C2AE; --edge:#E7E9E4; tiles as light
styles.figure_treatment: Every figure, human, comic or duo, gets the same umber fill. The edge marking is the only visual difference between builds. Group shows only as a small coloured floor tile under the feet and a swatch by the name.
styles.why: The strictest reading of 'builds differ only in their outline marking', and the marking is easiest to see because every fill matches. Held as the fallback if the reviewer finds group colours distracting. Rejected as the default because a skimming reader loses group membership at a glance.

picked_style: A. Studio wall. Family continuity with the Build Calculator (tokens, fonts, tape, status chips), the art's own wall and floor behind every lineup, and one fill per group from the turnaround palette, while the edge marking alone carries provenance. Note the choice for review: C (Umber print) is the fallback if group colour is judged to compete with the marking.
layout_desktop:
At 1280 px (max-width 1240, 16 px gutters):
- Tape strip across the top, as on the Build Calculator.
- Masthead in two columns. Left: kicker, BUILD COMPARISON in Big Shoulders 800, and the 4-line verdict at 19 px semibold. Right: a 3-line score explainer, then a 2x3 edge key (Solid, Dashed, Dotted, No edge, Hatched, Top of skull) with drawn samples.
- Sticky control bar: Height Same/Real, View Front/Side, and a "Go to" menu of stops on the right.
- The scale grid: a 330 px sticky rail and the stops column.
  - Rail (fills the viewport height): 34 px yellow log tape labelled 15/20/30/50/100/200/500/1000 with minor ticks, then six 21 px group lanes. Each build is a vertical range bar in its group colour, placed in sub-slots so bars don't overlap. Empty stretches are hatched bands labelled EMPTY. Kouri's 25 is a dashed ink line, the limits are a chalk dotted bracket over 40 to 200 rotated to read "LIMITS SOMEWHERE HERE?", and 924 is a chalk circle. A box marks the current stop. Stop labels sit at the right with leader lines, pushed apart so they don't collide, and a group legend sits under the rail.
  - Stops: lineups at 150 px skull height, about 6 per row (minmax 124 px), with captions under each figure. Duo and meatball at 230 px skull height, Rex and Ollie side by side.
- Tool section: two columns (5fr / 7fr). Left: sheet, inputs, checks. Right: results table, Copy results, target outline front and side.
- Footer with collapsed details.

The first screen at 1280x900 shows the masthead, the rail and the first row of six ordinary men.
layout_phone:
At 390 px (16 px gutters, no horizontal scroll, checked at scrollWidth 390):
- Tape strip, a 2-line mock banner (mock only), kicker, h1, a 5-line verdict lede, a 3-line score explainer, and the 6-item edge key in two columns.
- Sticky bar (52 px): "Height Same | Real" and "View Front | Side" as segmented controls. There is no Go-to menu on phone; the rail is the jump control.
- Scale grid: a 46 px sticky rail and a content column of about 300 px.
  - The rail sticks below the bar, height calc(100svh - 76px), min 520 px. It shows the tape with tick labels, a 14 px strip of build ticks in group colours, hatched gaps, the Kouri line, the chalk limits bracket at the right edge, the meatball circle and the current-stop box.
  - Lineups are 3 per row (minmax 88 px) at 86 px skull height. Each caption is a group swatch and short name, the score range in 17 px mono, a status chip, "FFMI x-y", and a red flag line where needed.
  - Rex and Ollie and the meatball use 140 px skull height, 2 per row (side view 1 per row because of the tails).
  - Gap stops are a hatched box, 92 px tall (160 px for the 188 to 924 stretch), labelled NO BUILDS HERE, with one line on what will fill it.
- Tool: stacked panels numbered 1 to 5 (a real sequence). Fields sit 2 per row, the results table is in its own overflow container, and the two target images sit side by side.

The first 844 px frame shows the verdict, the key, the controls, the top of the tape and the first heads. The mock phone page is about 11,900 px long.
axis:
One log axis, 15 to 1,000, drawn to scale only on the rail; the stops scroll in order but not to scale.

On the tape:
- Labelled majors at 15, 20, 30, 50, 100, 200, 500 and 1000.
- Minor ticks at 16 to 19, 25, 35, 40, 45, 60 to 90, 150, and 300 to 900.
- Each band appears in its stop's tag as 'Score 25 to 32', so position never depends on reading the gaps between stops.
- On desktop each build is a vertical range bar (low to high body fat) in its group lane; on phone, a tick at the geometric middle of its range.

Why not a broken axis: a break would hide the empty stretches the brief wants visibly empty. On the log tape the 188 to 924 stretch fills about 38% of the tape, and everything from 15 to 41 (about 45 of the 49 builds) fills about 24%. That proportion is the story. The stops give the crowded low end the room for figures that the to-scale tape can't.

Tapping the tape converts the tap's y back to a score and scrolls to that stop. Score ranges use an en dash and whole numbers below 100, rounded to 2 above 100, with no '≈'.
gaps_and_limits:
Empty gaps:
- They appear twice: as hatched rectangles across the lanes on the rail (labelled EMPTY on desktop), and as their own stops with the tag 'Score 41 to 57', the headline 'EMPTY', a verdict, a hatched box reading 'NO BUILDS HERE' and the line 'Step 2 adds figures drawn to order for this stretch, each labelled "measured from art".'
- The last gap, 'EMPTY TO THE TOP' (188 to 924), gets a taller box.
- Gap edges must be computed from the builds' range ends, never typed.

Natural limit:
- An anchor stop with no figures. Value rows read '25 · Kouri and others, 1995 [reported] · The highest of 74 drug-free lifters. The top of one sample, not a ceiling.', then 'Frame-based predictions (Casey Butt) [estimate] · fitted to pre-steroid champions; never tested in a study', then the Trexler line.
- In the mock, the Butt and Trexler values are placeholders. Reuse the Build Calculator's existing Kouri and Trexler facts.
- On the rail it is a dashed ink line at 25.

Functional limits:
- The stop 'Where the body stops working', tagged 'Score 40 to 200?'.
- It shows the Army median template with widths times 1, 1.5, 2 and 2.6 (scores 23, 51, 90, 152 in the mock), drawn as chalk-blue geometry with a [geometry] chip.
- Then three chalk-dashed rules, each with a '?' badge in place of a score:
  - Arms can no longer hang by the sides
  - Thighs touch all the way to the knee
  - Hands can no longer reach the face
- When the geometry is run, each '?' becomes the score and the rule also appears on the rail as a short chalk tick with that label.
- Until then the rail shows only the dotted 40 to 200 bracket.

Meatball:
- The last stop: a chalk-outlined circle as tall as the skull line, next to the Army median for scale, with caption '924 [geometry] 1,060 kg/m³ × π/6 × 0.925 × 1.8'. It is a chalk circle on the rail.
marking_key:
Every figure is a flat fill; only its edge changes. The edge is an ink stroke 3.8 px wide drawn under the fill, so about 1.9 px shows outside the shape on the wall.
- Solid (butt caps): the build's own number (measured, official or reported).
- Dashed 6/3.5: filled in from a template build.
- Dotted 0.1/4.2 (round caps): traced from art. Used for Rex and Ollie.
- No edge: head, hands and feet, which use average ANSUR proportions on every human.

Markings vary along one figure. figure.js bandEdges splits the body outline into neck, shoulders, chest, waist, hips, thigh and calf bands, each marked by its girth, and each arm segment takes its own girth's mark. Coleman has a solid chest, waist, arm and calf, a dashed forearm and neck, and a derived thigh that counts as own; that girth status is shown in the details. Comic characters are dashed all over.

Tails are drawn and excluded: a hatched fill (stripes in the figure's colour on the wall colour) with a thin dotted edge, and the caption line 'hatched tail: not counted'. Rex's front-view tail shows as a hatched patch between his legs; in side view both tails show in full.

Geometry is a chalk-blue outline with a pale chalk fill and a [geometry] chip; it is not a build.

Overstated or not comparable comic characters keep their score but get a red line under it:
- The Thing: 'Rock, not muscle. Overstated.'
- Colossus, steel: 'Steel skin. Not comparable.'
- Thor: 'Asgardian tissue is said to be denser. May be overstated.'
- Wolverine: 'Adamantium (about 45 kg) taken out.'
- Kingpin: 'Much of his weight is fat.'

Proposed but not in the mock: draw these as hollow bars on the rail.

Status of numbers: the Build Calculator's own chips (measured filled, official double, reported dashed, derived dotted, estimate dotted and hatched) sit beside every score. Scores at assumed body fat are 'estimate'; scores from measured or reported body fat are 'derived'.
controls:
One sticky bar at the top of the scale.
- Height: Same | Real (segmented, aria-pressed). Same scales every figure so the top of the skull sits on the dashed wall line. Real uses one metres scale for the whole page (30 px/m on phone, 52 px/m on desktop) with faint 1 m, 2 m and 3 m lines on the wall, so humans appear about 55 px tall beside 3 m Rex and Ollie.
- View: Front | Side. Side uses the template's side outline for humans and the traced side views for Rex and Ollie, tails hatched.
- Go to: a menu of stops at 720 px and wider.
- On phone: tap the tape to jump.

Proposed but not in the mock: tap a figure to open a details sheet with height, weight, body-fat range, each girth with its status and source link, and the figure drawn large so the edge marking reads.

State lives in the page. Only bare #anchors are used, for deep links to stops. localStorage may remember the Height and View choice, wrapped in try/catch.
tool_ui:
Section 'MEASURE A CHARACTER', separated from the scale by a heavy ink rule.
- Verdict: 'Upload a model sheet. Get volume, mass, seven girths and the score.'
- A chalk example note: 'Example loaded: Rex from duo.jpg, front view only. This is the tool's own test: it must land within the old methods' 2.52 to 2.60 m³.' The tool opens in a working state on its validation case, never on the turnarounds, which must not be measured in Step 1.

Steps (numbered because they are a real sequence):
1. The sheet: the image with dashed landmark lines (crest tip 3.048 m, top of skull, shoulder, waist, crotch, knee, ground) labelled at the edge, a 'Choose a sheet' file input, and the one-line spec 'Front, side and back at one scale, A-pose, plain background.' The full spec is in a details element.
2. Height and density: 'Height to top of skull' (m, hint 'Not crest or horn tips.'), 'Density' (kg/m³, hint 'Lean body, 1,020 to 1,080.') and 'Body fat' (% range, hint 'A range gives a score range.').
3. Checks: a list with Pass / Skip / Note / Fail tags.
   - 'Views differ in height by X%; limit 2%.'
   - 'Landmarks line up across views.'
   - 'No side view: depths come from ANSUR II depth-to-width ratios (soldiers, not dinosaurs).'
   - 'Slices are treated as ellipses. Girths can be off by 5 to 10%, volume by a few percent.'
4. Results, carrying the chip 'measured from art · estimate': a table grouped Size (volume ±3%, mass with range, frontal area), Score (muscle score range, plain FFMI), Girths ±5–10% (seven sites), and Segments (shoulder to elbow, elbow to wrist, hip to knee, and so on). A 'Copy results' button calls navigator.clipboard.writeText inside the click and falls back to selecting a hidden textarea; the copied text is a ready-to-paste builds.json entry.
5. Target outline: a 'Target score' input. The front and side outlines are drawn black on white with the five guide lines at the sheet spec, captioned 'front · score 60'. The note reads 'Shown at the sheet spec, 2,000 px tall. This page can't save files; the outline numbers can be copied instead.'

Recommend a node CLI in tools/ that writes the same PNGs locally for the collaborator.
copy:
Masthead
- Kicker: 'MUSCLE LEVEL, WITH HEIGHT TAKEN OUT'
- H1: 'BUILD COMPARISON'
- Lede: 'Ordinary men score about 22. The biggest bodybuilders reach about 40. Rex scores about 160 and Ollie about 180. The scale stops at 924: a solid ball of muscle.'
- Score line: 'The score is fat-free mass ÷ height³ × 1.8. That is the FFMI (fat-free kg ÷ height in m²) a body would have at 1.80 m tall. Body fat is mostly unknown, so each score is a range.'
- Edge key:
  - 'Solid: its own measurement'
  - 'Dashed: filled in from a template build'
  - 'Dotted: traced from art'
  - 'No edge: average head, hands, feet'
  - 'Hatched: drawn but not counted (tails)'
  - 'Top of skull: figures are scaled to it'

Stops (tag, then headline, then verdict)
- Score up to 25 / ORDINARY MEN: 'Average men score about 20 to 25. On their official stats, so do Superman and Batman.' Note: 'Bruce Banner, the Hulk at rest, is the slimmest build here. The soldiers are percentiles of each measure, not real people.'
- Score about 25 / THE NATURAL LIMIT: 'In one study of 74 drug-free lifters, nobody passed 25. That is the top of one sample, not a hard limit.'
- Score 25 to 32 / TRAINED HARD: 'Classic bodybuilders, big soldiers and study groups of competitors score 25 to 32.'
- Score 32 to 41 / THE BIGGEST HUMANS ON RECORD: 'Modern pro bodybuilders and strongmen top out near 40.' Note: 'Contest-day weights at very low body fat. Strongmen carry more fat, so their range is wider.'
- Score 41 to 57 / EMPTY: 'Nothing measured scores 41 to 57. No human and no comic character.'
- Score 57 to 88 / COMIC GIANTS: 'The heaviest comic characters score 57 to 88, if their official weight is muscle. For some it is not.' Note: 'Comic heights and weights are official. Their shapes are not: every girth is filled from a template, so every edge is dashed.'
- Score 40 to 200? / WHERE THE BODY STOPS WORKING: 'Somewhere between 40 and 200, the arms stop hanging, the thighs lock and the hands stop reaching the face. The exact scores are not worked out yet.' Note: 'Chalk-blue figures are geometry, not builds: the Army median with every width and depth scaled up. Each "?" becomes a score once the geometry is run.'
- Score 88 to 152 / EMPTY: 'Nothing scores 88 to 152. The jump across it is as big as from an ordinary man to Ronnie Coleman.' The comparison is computed from the score ratio (152/88 and 38.5/22.3 are both about 1.73) and must be recomputed from data.
- Score 152 to 188 / REX AND OLLIE: 'Rex scores about 160 and Ollie about 180: about twice the Hulk.' Note: 'Scored at 7.5% body fat (5 to 10%), height to the top of the skull, tails left out. Their crest and horns rise above the skull line.'
- Score 188 to 924 / EMPTY TO THE TOP: 'Nothing scores between Ollie and the ceiling.'
- Score 924 / THE MEATBALL: 'The scale stops at 924: a solid ball of muscle as tall as the figure.' Note: 'This is a chosen end point, not a law of geometry. A cube of muscle as tall would score more; no body could get there.'
- Every gap: 'NO BUILDS HERE' and 'Step 2 adds figures drawn to order for this stretch, each labelled "measured from art".'

Tool: 'MEASURE A CHARACTER' and 'Upload a model sheet. Get volume, mass, seven girths and the score.'

Rail (desktop): 'EMPTY' and 'LIMITS SOMEWHERE HERE?'.

Mock banner: 'MOCKUP. Outlines are real; every score is a rough placeholder, not checked.'
risks:
1. The meatball claim. The brief says 'a figure can't hold more volume than a ball as tall as itself'. That is false as geometry: a cylinder as tall holds 1.5 times as much and a cube about 1.9 times. The page must call 924 a chosen end point, as the mock does. Owner decision needed.

2. Only the rail is to scale; the stops are not. A reader could take the spacing between stops as distance. The mitigations are a numeric tag on every stop and the current-stop box on the rail.

3. The edge marking is subtle at phone size (86 px figures at 1x pixel density). Solid against dashed reads at 2x, but is weak at 1x. Real-height mode (humans about 55 px tall) makes it unreadable. The tap-for-details large view is needed. A test should check that the marking survives at 390 px.

4. Vocabulary clash with the sister page's status chips. Their borders use dashed for 'reported' and dotted for 'derived' and 'estimate', while the figure edges use dashed for template and dotted for traced from art. Words in both keys keep them apart. Alternative: give template a dash-dot pattern.

5. The [geometry] chip is outside the agreed status vocabulary (measured, official, reported, derived, estimate). It should be 'derived' in chalk colour. The lede's headline numbers also lack chips; add 'All scores here are estimates' or link each number to its stop.

6. Stop membership:
- Each build goes in the stop of its middle score, but ranges straddle edges (Luke Cage 38 to 41 against a gap starting at 41).
- Gap edges and the comparison sentences ('as big as from an ordinary man to Ronnie Coleman', 'about twice the Hulk') must be computed from data at build time, never typed.
- Every number in the mock comes from guessed body-fat ranges.

7. Natural-limit anchor values for Casey Butt and Trexler are placeholders. Reuse the Build Calculator's sourced Kouri and Trexler facts and source Butt properly, saying how weak its evidence is.

8. Page length. The phone mock is about 11,900 px, and Ordinary men and Trained hard hold 14 builds each. Collapsing to 'show all' would hide builds; consider a smaller phone figure size, or accept the length with the tap-to-jump tape.

9. Visual sameness:
- The comic giants all look alike because every one is one template scaled. That is honest, and the note says so, but it is repetitive.
- At high girths the template's arms merge into the torso; the seam hairline keeps them legible.
- Rex's front-view tail shows only as a hatched patch between his legs.

10. The sticky rail depends on 100svh inside the claude.ai frame. It falls back to min-height 520 and max 900. Check it in the published frame.

11. Tool:
- The mock's landmark line positions on duo.jpg are eyeballed.
- duo-validation.json's region polygons are generous boxes intersected with the mask, so they must not be drawn raw (they look misaligned).
- The viewer's sandbox blocks downloads, and long-press save of a data-URI image may not work either. The collaborator's GPT Images workflow needs the PNGs, so add a local node CLI.

12. Weight. The raw traced outlines make the inlined data about 1 MB; simplify the outlines with Ramer-Douglas-Peucker in the build.

13. Dark mode. The pale chalk fill of the geometry figures is low-contrast against the wall; the chalk outline carries it.

14. Fonts and tokens are reused from the sister page on purpose, for family. A reviewer wanting a distinct identity for this page should be pointed to styles.html.
